$comment: EHR 360 task library. Source of truth: Implementation Playbook v5, Section 4 master schedule. This file is DATA, editable without touching code. Fields: id, stream, title, owner (EHR|Cust|Joint), dueWeek (weeks before go-live; negative = after), dueDays (precise days before go-live, overrides dueWeek), gate (star items - the project does not advance past them), clock (build|external|post; default build), days OR durKey (duration; durKey scales via assumptions), deps (predecessor ids - only relationships that clearly exist), applies (declarative condition, see conditions.ts), note, ref. Conditions: {always}, {anyMove}, {mixedScope}, {moves:'sys'}, {stays:'sys'}, {type:['A','B']}, {submitterChanges}, {hasPrescribers}, {all/any/not}.

tasks.title: Hold kickoff; name project team and both customer roles
tasks.note: Clinical champion is a provider, not an administrator. Both customer roles named at kickoff, not mid-project.

tasks.title: Assign and record the implementation type using the four questions in §2.1
tasks.note: Without a recorded type, the difference between Type A and Type B is roughly five weeks of misallocated sequencing.

tasks.title: Issue the customer document request package and roster template
Execute BAA and complete the security review
Schedule the on-site discovery visit
tasks.note: Do not wait for the onboarding form to be returned before booking it.

tasks.title: Return the completed practice information sheet and provider roster
tasks.note: Hard gate on the rest of the build — nothing configures until practice and provider records exist.

tasks.title: Provision the practice tenant, environment and database
Complete the on-site discovery visit and capture the baseline
tasks.note: Denial rate, A/R aging, payer mix, claim volume, no-show rate, payer table condition. Once cutover occurs the pre-migration picture is gone permanently.

tasks.title: Build locations, departments and Place of Service mapping
Build provider records with NPI, DEA, license, taxonomy and PTAN
Supply the full staff list with names, emails, roles and site assignment
tasks.note: Resolve shared logins to named users — shared credentials break the audit trail and cannot be mapped one to one.

tasks.title: Document the manual bridges between any system staying and any system moving
tasks.note: Every move/stay pair is somebody re-keying data unless a spec says otherwise. Named owner per bridge.

tasks.title: Create user accounts and assign role-based security profiles
Confirm role permissions and approve the security matrix
Build provider schedule templates, sessions, blocks and holiday calendar
Load the fee schedule and charge master
Configure patient portal branding, self-scheduling rules and intake forms
tasks.note: Patients do not carry portal accounts across. Plan the re-invite wave.

tasks.title: Provide sample de-identified notes, three to five per provider
Provide the current visit type list with durations and scheduling rules
Provide the in-office procedure list with associated CPT codes
Provide the current superbill and CPT / ICD-10 preference lists
Build the service type catalogue
tasks.note: Service types come first — visit types map to them.

tasks.title: Export the existing .phrases / macro library from the legacy system
tasks.note: Where an export is available.

tasks.title: Build visit types mapped to service type, duration, template and charge list
Build provider note templates by specialty and by provider
tasks.note: From the practice's actual documentation, not a generic default set.

tasks.title: Build the shared practice .phrases library and load provider-personal .phrases
Build charge preference lists, order sets and favourite labs and imaging
Configure lab interfaces — practice provides reference lab account numbers
tasks.note: Standard labs interface path beyond reference lab accounts is Appendix C decision 6.

tasks.title: Configure document and fax routing rules, inbox queues and result routing
Provider review and sign-off on note templates and .phrases
Apply revisions from provider template review
Name at least one super user per site
Provide outside billing company contact, BAA, scope of work and user list
tasks.note: The outside biller is a project stakeholder, not an afterthought. Signed BAA before any access.

tasks.title: Publish the training calendar and send calendar invitations
Block protected training time and confirm coverage so staff are not double-booked
Load the training environment with practice configuration and sample patients
tasks.note: Train in a sandbox of the live environment — demo environments drift.

tasks.title: Deliver role-based training: provider, MA/clinical, front desk, biller
tasks.note: In the three weeks before go-live, never the final three days. Provider sessions first — highest risk, lowest availability.

tasks.title: Deliver super user and admin training
Distribute quick reference guides, recorded sessions and workflow one-pagers
Complete post-training competency checks; identify anyone needing a make-up
Deliver make-up and refresher sessions
Inventory all phone and fax numbers; confirm which port and which are retained
Request the CSR from the current carrier
Provide CSR, signed LOA, recent bill, account number, PIN and exact service address
tasks.note: Service-address mismatch against the carrier record is the most common port rejection.

tasks.title: Submit the port order to RingCentral
Provision the RingCentral account, extensions and interim numbers
Track the port order, resolve rejections, confirm the Firm Order Commitment date
tasks.note: Do NOT let the practice cancel the losing carrier before the port completes — cancellation releases the number.

tasks.title: Configure the ported number as outbound caller ID
Configure inbound fax delivery into the EHR fax inbox and assign routing queues
Configure fax cover sheet, outbound fax from within the chart, confirmation handling
Configure call routing, auto-attendant, ring groups, voicemail and after-hours
Test inbound fax to every routing queue and outbound fax from within a chart
Test outbound calling and confirm the correct caller ID is presented
Re-point existing RingCentral telephony and fax routing into EHR 360
tasks.note: Type B with telephony already live: re-point only — no port, but inbound fax and routing still move into EHR 360.

tasks.title: Confirm payment scope, POS terminal need and site count
Document Sola pricing in writing and obtain practice acknowledgment
tasks.note: Rate structure, per-transaction, monthly, terminal, chargeback, PCI — in writing before signature.

tasks.title: Provide bank account owner name and the email to send the application to
tasks.note: Only two items needed — the application goes out in week one.

tasks.title: Send the Sola application
Complete and submit the Sola application directly to Sola
Track merchant underwriting to approval; escalate anything stalled
Order POS terminals in the confirmed quantity per location
tasks.note: Merchant approval gates terminal ordering.

tasks.title: Receive terminals, confirm delivery and stage them at each site
Configure the Sola integration and map to payment posting
Configure copay collection at check-in and check-out, card-on-file, payment plans
Run a live test transaction, a void and a refund; confirm posting
Train front desk on terminal operation, receipts and end-of-day reconciliation
Collect the prescriber roster and open ePx identity proofing scheduling
tasks.note: Prescriber roster gates ePx accounts, which gate identity proofing, which gates EPCS.

tasks.title: Confirm which prescribers require EPCS and which schedules they prescribe
Name the two administrators for EPCS logical access control approval
Provide prescriber detail — legal name, NPI, DEA, cell phone, direct email
tasks.note: Legal name exactly as registered with the DEA. Cell phone required for identity proofing and second factor.

tasks.title: Create ePx accounts for every prescriber and prescribing agent
Book identity proofing sessions with each provider individually, by name
tasks.note: Track completion by named provider, not as a percentage.

tasks.title: Provide prescriber-agent relationships and preferred pharmacies
Every provider completes ePx identity proofing personally
tasks.note: Cannot be done on the provider's behalf. On the EXTERNAL clock: ~30 days per prescriber cohort, hardware tokens ship physically. Any implementation with prescribers is gated by this.

tasks.title: Enable EPCS and issue the second authentication factor; confirm token delivery
Two designated administrators complete the EPCS logical access control approval
Confirm identity proofing and EPCS at 100 percent, by named provider
Confirm state PDMP registration and configure PDMP access
Configure prescriber-agent relationships and refill request routing
Load pharmacy directory, set preferred pharmacies, enable formulary and benefit check
Enable medication history retrieval and configure patient consent handling
Send test prescriptions for each prescriber, including one controlled where EPCS is on
Verify refill request inbox routing and renewal response workflow
Confirm every prescriber can successfully transmit before go-live is approved
Reconcile controlled-substance recall intervals against the booked schedule
tasks.note: Fixed recall windows collide with a calendar booked out months during cutover.

tasks.title: CAQH refresh and roster attestation
Group NPI and payer credentialing applications, tracked to approval
tasks.note: 90–180 days where new, not compressible. If in scope, credentialing sets the billing-ready date — the go-live date moves, not the standard.

tasks.title: Verify payer contracts in effect under the existing TIN (§11a verify-only)
tasks.note: Contracts untouched on Types A/B — verify status and effective dates; do not re-credential.

tasks.title: Set up the practice on the clearinghouse; obtain submitter credentials
Provide the payer list with effective dates and provider-level credentialing status
Provide Medicare PTAN and Medicaid ID per provider and location
Stand up the enrollment tracker with separate 837, 835 and EFT columns per payer
tasks.note: A single column labelled EDI cannot answer whether remittance will route correctly. Three columns from day one.

tasks.title: Begin EDI submitter enrollment for all payers — 837, 835, EFT, eligibility
tasks.note: The single longest-lead item. Starts week one, before the build and before training. Every week of delay is a week of delayed cash flow after go-live.

tasks.title: Confirm whether the clearinghouse holds delegated or auto-enrollment coverage for any payers
tasks.note: OPEN DECISION 1b: where delegated coverage exists, no per-practice 837 form is needed. 835 and EFT usually still enroll individually.

tasks.title: Confirm the submitter of record structure — practices beneath one submitter, or enrolled individually
tasks.note: OPEN DECISION 1c: determines the true per-payer burden on §11b and therefore the billing-ready date.

tasks.title: Sign all payer enrollment forms and EDI agreements requiring practice signature
Provide the legacy payer table export for variant collapse and re-mapping
Identify where denials and clearinghouse notifications land today, and where they land after cutover
tasks.note: Invisible until the first denial after cutover fails to appear anywhere. Some payers send denials by fax or paper regardless of enrollment.

tasks.title: Collapse duplicate payer name variants and re-map to the clearinghouse payer list
tasks.note: A DEPENDENCY of enrollment tracking, not a parallel task — tracking is unreliable until variants are collapsed and re-mapped.

tasks.title: Decide the 835 receiver cutover point with billing, accounting for legacy A/R in flight
tasks.note: A DECISION, not a rule — both orders carry real risk. Record it with the billing lead named against it. See the ERA sequencing card.

tasks.title: Flag any payer with incomplete credentialing and agree a hold-billing plan
Provide contracted fee schedules and allowed amounts
Configure the clearinghouse connection and map payer IDs
tasks.note: Re-mapping cannot complete until the variant collapse is done.

tasks.title: Load contracted fee schedules and expected allowed amounts
Review the enrollment tracker per payer per transaction type; escalate anything unacknowledged
tasks.note: Weekly through T-1. Track per payer, per type — not in aggregate.

tasks.title: Provide self-pay, sliding scale and statement / collections policy
Configure claim scrubbing rules, edits and the rejection work queue
Configure ERA auto-posting rules, adjustment code mapping and denial routing
Configure the denial receiving point — 835 codes to worklist, faxed denials to a routing queue
tasks.note: Where two channels exist, name who reconciles them. An unlogged denial has no appeal and no timely-filing clock.

tasks.title: Test real-time eligibility against each major payer and confirm correct return
837 submitter enrollment approved across the payer list
tasks.note: Approves first, often within days for some payers. Its approval says nothing about 835 or EFT.

tasks.title: 835 ERA enrollment approved and receiver confirmed, payers covering 80% of collections
tasks.note: Routes through a different intake and commonly trails 837 by weeks. If 837 is live and 835 is not, go-live looks clean and the gap surfaces two to three weeks later.

tasks.title: EFT enrollment approved and deposit account confirmed
tasks.note: Frequently a separate form and sometimes a separate portal.

tasks.title: Configure patient statements, statement cycle and text-to-pay
Submit a test claim batch and confirm clean acceptance end to end
tasks.note: Accepted cleanly at both clearinghouse AND payer.

tasks.title: Agree the legacy A/R plan — who works it, in which system, and for how long
tasks.note: OPEN DECISION 5: every practice asks; answered case by case today. Two systems in parallel, potentially 90+ days.

tasks.title: Where 835 is not confirmed for a payer, brief the billing team to expect manual posting and flag early
Confirm legacy vendor export capability, cost and notice period
Check the incumbent contract notice window before serving termination notice
tasks.note: Read the auto-renewal clause first. Serving late costs a full term.

tasks.title: Secure legacy data access — export format specification and sample file delivered
tasks.note: Vendor-dependent, historically the largest variance in the plan. Nothing downstream is real until this lands.

tasks.title: Inventory the legacy address book — referring providers, pharmacies, labs, imaging
tasks.note: Routinely forgotten, and painful on day one when nobody can send a referral or a prescription to the right place.

tasks.title: Obtain written confirmation of legacy access end date, terms and cost
tasks.note: A belief about when access ends is not a plan. Anything not migrated becomes unrecoverable on that date. OPEN DECISION 4: should be a contract standard.

tasks.title: Agree and document migration scope — discrete versus PDF, by data element
tasks.note: OPEN DECISION 3: discrete vs PDF notes depends on the source EMR and determines whether staff re-key history after go-live. Say it before go-live, not after.

tasks.title: Confirm the test export and production export dates in writing with the legacy vendor
Build the field mapping specification and code crosswalks
tasks.note: Legacy data access gates field mapping.

tasks.title: Deliver the test export from the legacy system
Migrate a small sample batch of live patients for early visual validation
Consolidate the legacy payer table before import
tasks.note: Importing a fragmented payer table carries the problem forward permanently and breaks reporting on the new side.

tasks.title: Run the test import into the sandbox environment
Load the address book — referring providers, pharmacies, labs, imaging
Validate the test import — spot-check charts and confirm record counts
tasks.note: A provider who has not opened their own migrated chart has not validated.

tasks.title: Correct mapping issues identified in validation and re-run if required
Sign off on the test migration — no production import proceeds without this
Migrate future appointments onto the new visit types
tasks.note: Visit type build gates future-appointment migration.

tasks.title: Send a test referral and a test prescription to confirm the address book resolves
Confirm the legacy data entry freeze time and communicate it practice-wide
tasks.note: Anything entered after the freeze is re-keyed by hand on Monday.

tasks.title: Deliver the production export so data is available Friday
Run the production import across the weekend; reconcile record counts
tasks.note: Friday export → weekend import → Monday open. Not negotiable without moving the go-live date.

tasks.title: Confirm data available and correct before Monday open
Retain legacy system read-only access for the agreed period; verify it works
Provide triage protocols, phone scripts and nurse guidelines
Provide scheduling rules, new patient policy and provider preferences
Provide hours, holiday calendar, after-hours and on-call policy per site
Provide message routing rules, escalation criteria and escalation contacts
Provide walk-in, cancellation, no-show and late-arrival policies
Run the Rita rules discovery session with practice leadership and clinical staff
tasks.note: Source material is how the practice actually operates today, not how it would like to.

tasks.title: Document the practice rule set and obtain written confirmation
Configure triage logic, symptom routing and urgency classification
Configure scheduling rules, visit type routing and provider preferences
Configure hours, holiday calendar, after-hours handling and on-call escalation
Configure message queues, routing and response-time expectations
Configure escalation paths and notification recipients
Scenario-test Rita against the practice's real call and message patterns
Practice review and sign-off on Rita rules
Tune Rita rules against the first two weeks of live volume
Reduce the first-week schedule to 50 to 70 percent of normal volume
tasks.note: Those slots are already booked — the decision must be made early enough to act on.

tasks.title: Publish the hypercare support plan and escalation contacts
Hold the go / no-go call against Appendix B (Wednesday)
tasks.note: OPEN DECISION 1: the deciding authority is not designated. Name one before this call.

tasks.title: Run the full dress rehearsal — schedule, check in, document, prescribe, charge, collect, submit
Confirm all systems live — EHR, fax, phone, ePx, payments, clearinghouse (Sunday)
On-site or dedicated on-call support; daily morning huddle and end-of-day debrief
Review the issue log daily through week one
Twice-weekly check-in; template, .phrase and Rita refinement; refresher where adoption lags
Implementation review, open issue handoff, transition to standard support (week 4)
tasks.note: Planned-vs-actual by week feeds the duration assumptions — this is how estimates become observed data.

tasks.title: Monitor the first claim batch through to clearinghouse acceptance
Confirm the first ERA posts correctly and reconcile to the bank deposit
tasks.note: The first 835 posting run is where enrollment gaps finally show up.

tasks.title: Work legacy A/R per the agreed plan
Re-measure the discovery baseline at 60 to 90 days
tasks.note: The comparison that converts a satisfied practice into a referenceable one — only works if the baseline was captured at discovery.

tasks.title: Confirm the first Sola settlement deposits correctly to the practice account
